source_review.notes: Checked all six official sources. Kafka 4.2 design supports the described producer/broker/partition/offset/transaction delivery scopes and classic process-before/after-checkpoint loss/duplicate windows. AMQP 1.0 supports delivery state/settlement; MQTT 5.0 supports QoS handshakes, acknowledgements, sessions, expiry, and flow limits; current Pulsar concepts support subscriptions, individual/cumulative acknowledgements and redelivery features. Google Pub/Sub exactly-once and lease-management documentation supports the explicitly scoped pull-subscription acknowledgement/lease discussion. The chapter does not elevate any transport feature into arbitrary external-effect exactly-once semantics.

evidence: Checked logical message m/attempts a_i, producer P, broker B, delivery D, inbox I, effect E, acknowledgement/checkpoint C, workflow W_f, acknowledgement labels, effect state J, rates lambda/mu, in-flight L, processing W, lease/deadline/retry ages for consistent domains.
Confirmed implication, sequence, inequality, and Little's Law notation matches prose and stated assumptions.
Confirmed producer acceptance, delivery, ack/nack, lease, checkpoint, at-most/at-least/exactly-once scope, and durable application acceptance are separately defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation makes acknowledgement strength explicit rather than treating ack as a universal success.

Recomputed 500-concurrency ideal service as 500/0.4=1,250/s and backlog growth versus 2,000/s as 750/s before headroom/failure.
Checked batch offset 100-109 with failure at 104 implies highest contiguous completion 103 absent durable ownership semantics; counted ten examples/five exercise-answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Scenario rates, lease seconds, and offsets are examples rather than universal thresholds.

evidence: Constructed ack-before-effect crash trace proving possible loss.

symbolic_recomputation.notes: Reasoning separates delivery duplication from observationally idempotent business effects.

evidence: Reviewed client enqueue, broker leader/quorum ack, response loss, producer restart/outbox replay, duplicate publication, retention/expiry, and region failover.
Reviewed auto/individual/cumulative/batch ack, contiguous offsets, lease extend/loss/late ack, rebalance/stale owner, nack loops, poison, deadline, DLQ/redrive, and inbox backlogs.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans every adjacent crash window plus provider, application, external, operational, and adversarial boundaries.

evidence: Confirmed every guarantee names system/configuration/failure scope and every attempt retains logical identity/content.
Confirmed consumer ack follows earliest durable recoverable boundary, offsets remain contiguous, and stale lease owners are fenced.
Confirmed broker transactional/exactly-once features are not extended to unrelated stores/providers without participating protocols.
Confirmed retries/dead-letter preserve identity/key/sequence and application/effect backlogs remain observable after broker ack.
invariant_checking.notes: Dedup/effect retention is required to cover replay/redrive horizon for claimed protection.

evidence: Reviewed classic ack/effect ordering proof and confirmed each ordering leaves loss or duplicate window unless atomicity/idempotency/recovery bridges it.
Reviewed batch contiguous-checkpoint argument and confirmed maximum-seen commit loses unresolved holes.
Reviewed inbox argument and confirmed ack transfers, rather than eliminates, work/backlog ownership.
Reviewed external timeout argument and confirmed response loss requires stable provider effect ID/outcome query or leaves residual risk.
proof_review.notes: Proof claims remain scoped and avoid unqualified end-to-end exactly-once language.

evidence: Confirmed Kafka/AMQP/MQTT/Pulsar/PubSub protocol and feature semantics are attributed and configuration scoped.
Confirmed producer acceptance, broker durability, delivery, application acceptance, local effect, external outcome, and workflow completion labels are distinct.
Confirmed transport exactly-once/QoS, transactional pipelines, local idempotent transitions, and business effects use precise noninterchangeable claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative provider behavior, design mechanisms, and application/domain assurances remain distinct.

Little's Law and capacity values are labeled stable-system/scenario estimates.
Actual broker durability, lease behavior, duplicate rates, store atomicity, provider idempotency, backlog capacity, failover, and SLOs remain explicit integration/load/fault evidence obligations.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed acknowledgement ladder, producer recovery, delivery guarantee scopes, consumer boundaries, checkpoints/batches, leases, retry/expiry, local and external effects, capacity/backpressure, control security, observability, and fault verification as one end-to-end model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through outbox, stable publication IDs, inbox/local state/outbox transactions, contiguous completion trackers, progress-based leases/fencing, classified retry/DLQ, effect ledgers/provider queries, bounded prefetch, multi-backlog telemetry, and crash-window tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins with observable acknowledgement boundaries, develops delivery models and crash windows, then applies them to databases, external effects, capacity, and operations. Ten examples isolate distinct scopes; five exercises progress from labeling/arithmetic to stream, long-job, and payment designs with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
